opportunity.title: FEMA's Deployment Management Solution (Sources Sought)
opportunity.description: FEMA is conducting market research for commercial off-the-shelf, configurable COTS, custom or hybrid solutions to replace the legacy Deployment Tracking System and improve incident workforce management: readiness, personnel availability, qualifications, certifications, training, deployment tracking, incident and event staffing, force packages, equipment assignment, reporting and analytics, secure cloud hosting, and interoperability with FEMA and DHS systems. Estimated value is $50 million to $100 million over five to ten years. Questions were due Oct 5, 2026.

profile._note: FICTIONAL SAMPLE COMPANY for scenario testing. Not a real firm. Past performance and staffing are invented; only the NAICS codes, set-aside definitions and every opportunity and award figure used against it are real public data.

profile.pastPerformance: Service-disabled veteran-owned. Prime on two VA software maintenance contracts (about $2.1M and $3.4M) and one Army National Guard web portal ($650K).
profile.capacityNotes: Twenty-two staff. Active facility clearance (Secret). SOC 2 Type II report current. Strong VA customer references.
verification: NAICS codes confirmed against USAspending reference (api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/references/naics) on 2026-10-16.
Set-asides follow SBA definitions: SBA = small business, 8A = 8(a) Business Development, HUBZONE, WOSB/EDWOSB, SDVOSB.

checks.reason: Full and open competition; no set-aside required.
NAICS 541511 is in the company's codes.
Place of performance DC is within the company's coverage.

rationale.point: Incumbent contract value ($58.3M) and duration through 2027 indicate a high barrier for a small business with maximum prior prime of $3.4M.

The system's focus on incident workforce management for disaster response (Claim 2) is not directly evidenced in the company's past performance (VA software maintenance, Army National Guard web portal).
Sources Sought with no set-aside allows the company to respond and advocate for a small business or SDVOSB set-aside, given DHS has awarded 153 small business set-asides in this NAICS.
Company's current capacity (22 staff, Secret clearance) may support a subcontracting role but not a prime on a $58M effort without significant teaming.

risks: Incumbent advantage and contract size mismatch
Lack of direct domain past performance in disaster response workforce management
Full and open competition against large integrators
Capacity constraints for prime role on a $58M+ contract
nextSteps: Respond to Sources Sought highlighting SDVOSB status, relevant software maintenance experience, and Secret clearance
Explore teaming with larger prime or incumbent for subcontracting opportunities
Monitor for solicitation and evaluate set-aside decision before committing bid resources
Assess ability to scale staffing for disaster response workforce management
